# infisical_pam_account_mongodb (Resource)

Create and manage MongoDB accounts in Infisical PAM. The connection is tested when the account is created or its connection changes. Only Machine Identity authentication is supported for this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    infisical = {
      # version = <latest version>
      source = "infisical/infisical"
    }
  }
}

provider "infisical" {
  host = "https://app.infisical.com" # Only required if using self hosted instance of Infisical, default is https://app.infisical.com
  auth = {
    universal = {
      client_id     = "<machine-identity-client-id>"
      client_secret = "<machine-identity-client-secret>"
    }
  }
}

data "infisical_gateway" "main" {
  name = "prod-gateway"
}

resource "infisical_pam_folder" "dbas" {
  name = "dbas"
}

resource "infisical_pam_account_template" "mongodb" {
  name         = "mongodb"
  account_type = "mongodb"
  gateway_id   = data.infisical_gateway.main.id
}

resource "infisical_pam_account_mongodb" "orders" {
  name        = "orders-admin"
  folder_id   = infisical_pam_folder.dbas.id
  template_id = infisical_pam_account_template.mongodb.id

  connection_details = {
    connection_string = "mongodb://mongo-1.internal:27017,mongo-2.internal:27017/?replicaSet=rs0"
    database          = "orders"
    ssl_certificate   = file("mongo-ca.pem")
  }

  credentials = {
    username = "orders_admin"
    password = var.orders_admin_password
  }
}

variable "orders_admin_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connection_details` (Attributes) How to reach the MongoDB target. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connection_details))
- `credentials` (Attributes) The credentials of the account. Secrets are never read back, so changes made outside of Terraform, such as rotation, aren't detected. To stop managing a secret, add it to `lifecycle.ignore_changes` instead of removing it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `folder_id` (String) The ID of the folder the account is in. Changing it moves the account.
- `name` (String) The name of the account, unique in its folder. Must be lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, at most 64 characters.
- `template_id` (String) The ID of the account template the account uses, which must be a `mongodb` template.

### Optional

- `description` (String) An optional description of the account.
- `gateway_id` (String) The ID of the gateway to connect through instead of the template's.
- `gateway_pool_id` (String) The ID of the gateway pool to connect through instead of the template's.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the account.

<a id="nestedatt--connection_details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `connection_details`

Required:

- `connection_string` (String) The `mongodb://` or `mongodb+srv://` URI of the deployment, with options such as `replicaSet` in its query string. It must not include credentials or a database.

Optional:

- `database` (String) The database to connect to, which is also where the user authenticates unless the connection string sets `authSource`. Defaults to `admin`.
- `ssl_certificate` (String) The PEM-encoded CA certificate to verify the server with.
- `ssl_enabled` (Boolean) Whether to connect over TLS, which `mongodb+srv://` deployments such as Atlas need. Defaults to true. Set it to false for a server without TLS, since a mismatch makes the connection test time out.
- `ssl_reject_unauthorized` (Boolean) Whether to reject a server certificate that isn't trusted. Defaults to true.


<a id="nestedatt--credentials"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Required:

- `username` (String) The database user.

Optional:

- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the database user.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# This will import the MongoDB PAM account by its ID.
# Secrets are never read back, so set the password in the configuration after importing.
terraform import infisical_pam_account_mongodb.example <account_id>
```
